prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed is a correction container of a Marinelli, wherein a first groove is formed in the lower portion of the container body formed with a diameter corresponding to the inner diameter of the lower surface of the Marinelli beaker, to be attached to a detector of a detecting system for nuclide analysis, a second groove having a diameter smaller than that of the first groove is formed on the upper portion, and an intake and exhaust hole is formed through the first groove to the second groove. According to the present invention, a Marinelli beaker covers a upper portion of a container body to wrap around it, and a detector of a nuclide detecting device is inserted into a first groove formed in a lower portion of the container body. By means of the correction container according to the present invention, the distance between the position of radionuclides in the sample in a Marinelli beaker and the detector is maintained constant. Accordingly, the reliability of the detection value in nuclide analysis is advantageously improved.

A correction container for a Marinelli beaker is described. The container body has a lower section provided with a first groove whose diameter corresponds to the inner diameter of the lower surface of the Marinelli beaker, so that the container can be mounted on a detector of a nuclide analysis detection system. An upper section of the container body includes a second groove with a smaller diameter than the first groove, and an intake/exhaust hole extends from the first groove to the second groove.

outputs.L3:
The invention discloses a correction container for a Marinelli beaker used in a nuclide analysis detecting system. The correction container is designed to improve the accuracy and reliability of nuclide detection by maintaining a stable and consistent positional relationship between a sample containing radionuclides and a detector.

The correction container includes a container body. A first groove is formed in a lower portion of the container body. The first groove is sized and shaped to correspond to the inner diameter of the lower surface of the Marinelli beaker, and is configured to receive a detector used in the nuclide analysis detecting system. By allowing the detector to be positioned within the first groove, the correction container helps ensure that the detector is properly aligned with the Marinelli beaker during measurement.

A second groove is formed in an upper portion of the container body. The second groove has a diameter smaller than that of the first groove. This stepped groove structure allows the correction container to be fitted appropriately with the Marinelli beaker while defining a controlled space for positioning the sample and detector relative to one another.

In addition, an intake and exhaust hole is provided in the container body. The intake and exhaust hole extends through the container body from the first groove to the second groove, thereby allowing air to enter and exit during installation, removal, or use of the correction container. This feature facilitates smooth assembly and helps prevent pressure imbalance or air trapping between the container, the Marinelli beaker, and the detector.

Through this configuration, the correction container keeps the distance between radionuclides contained in a sample and the detector constant during nuclide analysis. As a result, variations in detection geometry are reduced, measurement conditions become more uniform, and the reliability of nuclide detection values is improved.
outputs.L4:
A Marinelli correction container is a specially designed auxiliary container used in radionuclide measurement systems to improve the consistency and reliability of nuclide analysis. The container is configured to be installed between a Marinelli beaker, which holds a sample containing radionuclides, and a nuclide detection system, such as a gamma-ray detector. Its structure allows the detector and the sample container to be arranged in a fixed and repeatable geometry during measurement.

The correction container includes a body provided with stepped grooves. These grooves are formed at different levels or diameters so that the container can be accurately fitted to the shape of the Marinelli beaker and the detection device. In particular, a lower groove is provided to receive and position the detector in a predetermined location. By seating the detector in this defined groove, the detector is held at a stable and reproducible position relative to the sample contained in the Marinelli beaker.

The container may also include an intake and exhaust hole. This hole allows air, gas, or pressure to be released or introduced when the Marinelli beaker and the correction container are assembled or separated. As a result, the container can be attached and removed more easily, while also helping to prevent unstable mounting caused by trapped air or pressure differences.

When the Marinelli correction container is used, the distance between the radionuclides distributed in the sample and the detector is kept constant. This is important because detection efficiency can vary depending on the distance and geometry between the radioactive sample and the detector. If the detector position changes from one measurement to another, the measured radiation intensity may fluctuate even when the actual radioactivity of the sample remains the same.

By maintaining a fixed measurement geometry, the Marinelli correction container reduces measurement error and improves reproducibility. It helps ensure that radionuclide analysis is performed under consistent conditions, thereby increasing the reliability of the detected values and the accuracy of quantitative analysis. This makes the container useful in environmental radioactivity testing, laboratory nuclide analysis, quality control measurements, and other applications requiring precise and repeatable radiation detection.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent abstract for an invention called a correction container for a Marinelli beaker used in radionuclide analysis, including grooves, an intake/exhaust hole, detector insertion, and the benefit of maintaining a constant distance to improve reliability.
counterfactuals.output: A correction container for a Marinelli beaker used in radionuclide analysis is provided. The correction container includes a container body configured to receive the Marinelli beaker and to be positioned around a radiation detector inserted into a central insertion portion of the Marinelli beaker. Grooves are formed in the container body to guide and stabilize placement of the Marinelli beaker, and an intake/exhaust hole is provided to allow air to enter or exit during insertion and removal, thereby preventing pressure imbalance and facilitating smooth handling. The container is configured to maintain a constant distance between a sample contained in the Marinelli beaker and the detector during measurement. By ensuring reproducible positioning and spacing, the correction container reduces measurement variation and improves the reliability and accuracy of radionuclide analysis.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a Korean-style English patent summary describing a Marinelli correction container with a lower first groove matching the detector/beaker diameter, an upper second groove of smaller diameter, and a through hole connecting them.
counterfactuals.output:
A Marinelli correction container is disclosed. The Marinelli correction container includes a container body having a predetermined height and defining an internal space for accommodating a sample or correction material. A first groove is formed in a lower portion of the container body and is recessed upward from a bottom surface of the container body. The first groove has a diameter corresponding to a diameter of a detector or a beaker, so that the detector or the beaker can be stably inserted into or positioned relative to the container body.

A second groove is formed above the first groove and has a diameter smaller than the diameter of the first groove. The second groove is arranged coaxially or substantially coaxially with the first groove. A through hole is formed between the first groove and the second groove so as to connect the first groove and the second groove to each other. Accordingly, the Marinelli correction container can provide a structure suitable for calibration or correction measurement while maintaining an alignment relationship with the detector or beaker.

By providing the lower first groove corresponding to the diameter of the detector or beaker, the upper second groove having a smaller diameter, and the through hole connecting the grooves, the Marinelli correction container improves mounting stability, measurement reproducibility, and correction accuracy in radiation measurement using a Marinelli-type geometry.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical disclosure paragraph for a nuclide analysis device accessory: a container body fitted inside a Marinelli beaker, with grooves for detector placement and airflow, explaining how it stabilizes sample-to-detector geometry.
counterfactuals.output: A nuclide analysis device accessory includes a container body configured to be removably fitted within an interior cavity of a Marinelli beaker, the container body defining a fixed sample-receiving volume and one or more positioning grooves formed on an inner or outer surface thereof. The grooves are dimensioned to receive and locate at least a portion of a radiation detector, detector housing, guide member, or spacer so that, when the container body is installed in the Marinelli beaker, the relative position between the sample and the detector is maintained at a predetermined geometry. Additional groove portions, channels, or recesses may be provided to form airflow paths between the container body and the Marinelli beaker, thereby permitting air displacement during insertion, removal, filling, or sealing and reducing void formation or pressure-induced movement of the sample. By mechanically constraining the container body within the Marinelli beaker and providing repeatable detector-placement features, the accessory minimizes variations in sample height, radial spacing, detector insertion depth, and sample-to-detector distance, thereby improving counting reproducibility, calibration transferability, and nuclide analysis accuracy.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Please produce an abstract in patent language for a Marinelli beaker calibration/correction container that wraps with the beaker, receives a detector in a lower groove, and improves radionuclide detection accuracy.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus for calibrating and correcting radionuclide measurements obtained with a Marinelli beaker is disclosed. The apparatus comprises a correction container configured to conform to and at least partially wrap around an exterior portion of the Marinelli beaker, the correction container defining a sample-receiving volume positioned relative to the beaker to provide a predetermined calibration geometry. A lower portion of the correction container includes a groove or recess dimensioned to receive at least a portion of a radiation detector, thereby locating the detector in a repeatable position with respect to the Marinelli beaker and the calibration material disposed in the correction container. The conforming wrap configuration and detector-receiving groove reduce geometric uncertainty, improve reproducibility of detector-to-sample spacing, and facilitate correction for attenuation, background, efficiency, or geometry-dependent measurement effects. Use of the correction container thereby enhances the accuracy and reliability of radionuclide detection and activity determination for samples measured in the Marinelli beaker.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
